heuristics: H1 (random-function model): with published pseudorandom constants c_j = sha512(...) mod r, walker states collide at the parallel-rho birthday rate t^2/(2(r-1)), distinguished-point counts are Binomial(t, 2^-32), and cycle entries occur at the self-pair birthday scale t^2/(2Kr) = 1.717e-05 with expected waste 8.731e-11 of the budget, converted by Markov's inequality to P(waste exceeds 2^-23 of the budget) <= 7.32e-04, with reseed work charged inside the same bound. No rescaling of the scalar confines the step set: Part A measures every M <= 2^12 (narrowest window 0.6329 of r, and the same check detects the rejected v6 constants at 5.93e-67) and the counting heuristic 32*W^31/r^30 puts expected confiners of width <= 2^240 below 2^-235.

Efficiency (collision-time factor): within the fixed budget the success probability is 1 - exp(-(1.5/c)^2/2) under Rayleigh collision times, so the 0.39 claim holds for every factor c <= 1.5086. Teske's measured r-adding factors for r >= 16 are at most ~1.1x the ideal, giving modeled success 0.6053484543 >= 0.39; the toy implies c = 1.014. The claim is made against the factor tolerance, not against the toy measurement.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold (modeled success 0.6053484543 at Teske's measured collision-time factor 1.1; the claim tolerates every factor up to 1.5086).
The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^98-slot allocation (2^105 bytes); overflow aborts with probability <= exp(-2^95.6) under H1, subtracted.

Standard cryptanalysis (parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points and pseudorandom published constants); the confinement analysis (executed rescaling certificate plus counting bound) and the itemized full-coverage ledger are the contribution under this cost model.
